MSC Divina Review

Review of MSC Divina

The 2012-built MSC Divina cruise ship is the third of MSC’s Fantasia-class liners, with sisterships Fantasia, Preziosa, and Splendida.

The vessel (IMO number 9585285) is currently Panama-flagged (MMSI 373178000) and registered in Colon.

History - Construction and Ownership

MSC Cruises (MSC Crociere) is a passenger shipping company headquartered in Genoa and Naples, established in 1960. Today, MSC Crociere is a subsidiary of MSC (Mediterranean Shipping Company), the world’s 2nd largest container shipping company. MSC Crociere is the world’s largest privately owned cruise company.

By annual passenger volumes, MSC ranks as the world’s 3rd largest cruise shipowner, following only Carnival Corporation and RCG-Royal Caribbean Group.

In 2014, MSC announced that its four Lirica-class ships were scheduled for major renovations under the line’s “Renaissance Programme.” In 2015, the company ordered four new ships from STX France and Fincantieri Italy, with an option for three additional units. The first two vessels were scheduled for delivery in 2017 – Meraviglia in May and Seaside in November.

The 4000-passenger MSC Divina is among the largest ships in the MSC fleet. Her design impresses not only with size but also with layout – over 80% of all cabins offer ocean views, and many feature private step-out balconies.

Decks and Cabins

MSC Divina staterooms (1751 total, in 12 grades) include 99 Suites, 1133 Balcony cabins, 116 Oceanview cabins, and 405 Inside cabins. Most accommodations are Balcony cabins (190 ft2 / 18 m2) with 40 ft2 / 4 m2 balconies. The largest accommodations are the Yacht Club Royal Suites (400 ft2 / 37 m2, with 170 ft2 / 16 m2 wraparound terraces).

The vessel has 17 decks, of which 14 are passenger-accessible and 9 contain cabins. Decks are named after Greek gods and goddesses.

Shipboard Dining Options – Food and Drinks

The ship offers two main dining rooms. MSC Divina’s primary restaurant spans two decks, and an additional panoramic restaurant – Texmex – features an open kitchen. Other venues include a French à la carte restaurant, a pizzeria, and a wine bar offering gourmet selections.

Below is the full list of MSC Divina’s restaurants and food bars:

  • The Black Crab Restaurant (2-tier forward dining room on Decks 5 & 6; capacity 521 seats / 1080 m2 on Deck 5 and 731 seats / 907 m2 on Deck 6; open for breakfast 7–10 am, lunch 12–2 pm, and dinner with two fixed seatings at 7 and 9:45 pm; regional Italian menus nightly, 7-course dinner, vegan/vegetarian options)
  • Villa Rossa Restaurant (aft dining room, capacity 738 seats, Mediterranean cuisine; open for breakfast 7–10 am, lunch 12–2 pm, and fixed dinner seatings at 7 or 9:45 pm; 1227 m2, Deck 6)
  • Sports Lounge & Bar (57-seat sports bar with large TVs, two 10-pin bowling lanes; serves American, Spanish, Chinese, German, and Oriental selections; à la carte surcharge; open 4 pm–1 am; 148 m2, Deck 7)
  • Caffe Italia (58-seat specialty coffee bar with complimentary cookies and pastries; à la carte surcharge; 258 m2, Deck 7)
  • La Cantina di Bacco (110-seat Italian pizzeria and wine bar; open 1 pm–2 am; 340 m2, Deck 7)
  • Butcher’s Cut (96-seat steakhouse with exclusive Chef’s Table; fixed-charge menu €49 pp or à la carte options; open for brunch on sea days, lunch, and dinner; 435 m2, Deck 7)
  • Calumet and Manitou Buffets (Deck 14; 475 seats / 1288 m2 forward, 451 seats / 882 m2 aft; self-service cafeterias open 6 am–3 am; multiple food stations including Grill, Pasta, Pizza, Carving, Ethnic, Mediterranean, Bakery, Kids Corner)
  • Le Muse Restaurant (110-seat aft dining room on Deck 15, exclusive for MSC Yacht Club guests; gourmet French and Italian cuisine; all food and beverages included; 218 m2)
  • Galaxy Restaurant / Lounge & Disco (50-seat à la carte specialty venue, dinner 6–10:30 pm and brunch 10 am–1:30 pm; nightclub with full bar; 421 m2, Deck 16)

Shipboard Entertainment Options – Fun and Sport

MSC Divina offers a wide range of entertainment and leisure facilities, including a casino, 4D cinema, library, show lounge, disco, Internet café, and virtual reality center. The tiered Pantheon Theatre provides multilingual entertainment. Sports facilities include five pools, a fitness center, SPA, sauna, and twelve Jacuzzis. There is also a Formula 1 simulator.

Below is the complete list of lounges, clubs, and entertainment venues for kids, teens, and adults:

  • Medical Center (infirmary, 284 m2, Deck 4; staffed 24/7 by onboard doctors and nurses; payments via boarding pass; travel insurance recommended)
  • Divina Atrium (five-deck-high central area with live entertainment, Deck 5)
  • Reception (119-seat guest services desk, 489 m2, Deck 5)
  • Divina Bar (28-seat lobby bar, 120 m2, Deck 5)
  • Cybercafe (15-computer Internet room, 52 m2, Deck 5)
  • Pantheon Theatre (1511 seats; grand-style performances; two nightly shows at 8 pm and 10:15 pm; 2086 m2, Decks 5/6)
  • Casino Veneziano (213 seats; slot machines, table games; smoking allowed; full bar; 1017 m2, Deck 6)
  • Poker Room (Texas Hold’em lounge adjacent to the casino)
  • Video Games Arcade (55 m2, Deck 6)
  • The Cigar Lounge & Bar (31-seat smoking lounge with premium liquors; 85 m2, Deck 6)
  • Piazza Del Doge (109-seat Venetian-style square with live music, ice cream, coffee, cocktails, pastries; à la carte charges apply; 460 m2, Deck 6)
  • Mini Mall / Duty-Free Shop (53 m2, Deck 6)
  • La Boutique (fashion shop, 76 m2, Deck 6)
  • Il Gioiello (jewelry and accessories, 62 m2, Deck 6)
  • Silver Lounge (98-seat lounge with live music, 392 m2, Deck 6)
  • Excursions Office (10-seat shore excursion desk, 100 m2, Deck 6)
  • L’Angolo dell’Oggetto (accessories and gift shop, 43 m2, Deck 6)
  • La Caramella (sweets and toys, 30 m2, Deck 6)

Itineraries

MSC Divina’s itinerary program is based on 7-day Caribbean cruises from Miami FL and 7-day Western Mediterranean sailings from Civitavecchia-Rome, Naples, and Barcelona. Divina also operates low-cost Transatlantic repositioning crossings between Europe and Florida.

In 2019, a fleet of three MSC ships offered Caribbean roundtrips from Miami: Seaside, Meraviglia, and Divina.

In early June 2020, MSC announced that in 2021 Divina would be homeported at Port Canaveral, Florida for 3- to 7-night roundtrips departing Thursdays and Sundays. Port Canaveral is considered the cruise port to Orlando – one of the USA’s most visited tourist destinations and home to Walt Disney World.

  • Divina’s maiden voyage from Port Canaveral departed on September 16, 2021 – also her first commercial sailing after the COVID-19 pause.
  • The itineraries (3/4/7 nights) visited ports in The Bahamas (Nassau, MSC Ocean Cay) and Mexico (Cozumel, Costa Maya).
  • Divina homeported in Port Canaveral between Sept 16 and Nov 21, 2021, then repositioned to Miami.
  • The next Port Canaveral season began on April 8, 2022.
  • The voyages can be combined into back-to-back cruises of 10, 11, or 14 nights.

MSC Divina Wiki

The vessel (STX France, Chantiers de l’Atlantique yard / hull number U32) has a volume of 139072 GT, DWT (deadweight tonnage) of 13188 tons, and a maximum draught of 8.7 m. The powerplant consists of GE Power Conversion marine diesel engines (Converteam model 16V46C) with a combined output of 43.7 MW (58,600 hp). The registered shipowner is COMPANIA NAVIERA MERAVIGLIA SA, and the registered manager is MSC CROCIERE SA.

Divina is the largest Fantasia-class MSC liner, with sisterships Fantasia, Preziosa, and Splendida. One of the newest and largest MSC vessels (inaugural cruise May 27, 2012), Divina was originally ordered as “MSC Fantastica” and later renamed in honor of the actress Sophia Loren.

The “Sophia Loren” Royal Suite—designed for and with her involvement—is Suite 16007 (category YC3 “Yacht Club Royal Suite”), located on Deck 16.

MSC Divina Refurbishments Review

Drydock 2025

The vessel’s most recent drydocking took place in April 2025 at the Palumbo Shipyard in Valletta.

The project focused on regularly scheduled maintenance works, technical and safety/classification inspections, and hull cleaning and repainting.
